title.narrative: Youth Empowerment For Better Communities (Qeyadah) Projec

description.narrative:
the project has been designed so that the activities provide a strong foundation for young people participating in the project as well as for future students at the University of Jordan to take on this role. Learning in a classroom is insufficient on its own. Instead, students are supported to put their learning into pratcice, developing their ideas into functional products, projects and initiatives while being supported and guided via mentoring. Incorporating community feedback means communities will feel a sense of ownership of the solutions developed by the students. this sense of ownership ensures communities feel empowered, thus supports positive community attitudes towards implementing and adopting the students' solutions with members taking action to ensure success.

The project has synergies with other initiatives focused on harnessing the energies of young people as agents of change and devlopment. The university of Jordan has several EU funded projects focused on Innovation and youthempowerment/ employment. Learning from the "mEquity- Imporving Higher Education Quality in Jordan using Mobile Technologies for Better Integration of Disadvantaged Groups to Socio-economic Diversity" and the EDU4ALL projects will be valuable for supporting and enhancing Equality integration in the project, and for guiding student ideas addressing equality needs/ challenges related to sustainable development.

The innovation and entrepreneurship center at the university of Jordan has successfully run boot camps, competitions, and training programmes supporting students to develp ideas: The Campus Development Ideathon, which supported students to generate ideas related to the needs of the university of Jordan to improve campus life is particulary relevant.

The target group of beneficiaries are young people regardless of disability and gender, studying at the university of Jordan campuses. It is anticipated that students in their 2nd year of university will be chosen to take part in this project.

Final beneficiaries are members of the community who have students studying at the university of Jordan campuses in Amman and Aqaba.
